title: Vickers Wellington DV717
memorial_details: Plain, rectangular, metal (possibly aluminium) plaque mounted on a light-wood backboard. Commemoration is in black, upper-case letters.
inscription: Upper plaque: WELLINGTON BOMBER dv 717 MARK C CREWED BY RNAF/ CRASHED ON A TRAINING EXERCISE ATBRECKS FARM/ MAPLEBECK 15TH OCTOBER 1942/ ALL AIRCREW KILLED AND LAID TO REST IN OLLERTON CEMETERY (SGT MCCORD IN ARGDAGH, IRELANND0/ CREW ...... AGE/ (names)/ Lower plaque: KA MMAUMAHARA TONU TATOU KI A RATOU/ WE WILL REMEMBER THEM

sources.title: Facebook post by Adrian Gray (Notts Local History Association), Southwell Local History group — identifies location between Maplebeck and Eakring near Hagley's Dumble

narrative: Wellington DV717 Mark C, crewed by the Royal New Zealand Air Force (RNAF), crashed on a training exercise at Brecks Farm, Maplebeck, Nottinghamshire on 15 October 1942. All five crew were killed. Four are buried at Ollerton Cemetery; Sgt McCord was buried in Argadagh, Ireland. The lower plaque carries the Māori phrase 'Ka maumahara tonu tātou ki a rātou' — 'We will remember them'. A local history post by Adrian Gray (Notts Local History Association) records the memorial as standing beside a woodland avenue on the footpath between Maplebeck and Eakring, near Hagley's Dumble.
community_connection: The memorial beside a woodland path between Maplebeck and Eakring was recorded by Adrian Gray of the Nottinghamshire Local History Association, whose post in the Southwell Local History group brought it to wider attention. The lower plaque carries the Māori farewell, reflecting the New Zealand nationality of the crew.
